_comment: Named serving backends. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be listed here
and then addressed by name: --backend ollama, --backend npu, ...
'ollama' is the backend this stack's docker-compose.yml brings up and is
the default. The geniex-* entries are Windows-host lanes reached from WSL2
Optional per-entry fields, all honoured by bench_cli.post_json (one request path for every tool):

api_key_env    Name of the environment variable holding the API key. The KEY NEVER GOES IN THIS FILE. Sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <value>'; an unset or empty variable aborts the run naming the variable, and the value is never printed or written to a report.
headers        Extra request headers as a JSON object, merged after Content-Type and before the Authorization header (so api_key_env always wins). Only the header NAMES reach a report.

request_extra  JSON object merged into the request body BEFORE the caller's own keys, so an explicit model/max_tokens/temperature always wins. One level deep. Use it for per-backend knobs: {"num_ctx": 16384} on Ollama, {"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}} on a Qwen server.

probe          Default true. false stops the tools asking /v1/models what this endpoint serves -- set it on paid hosts, where a discovery request costs money or is not offered. A probe:false backend must name its 'model' here or be given --model.

A 'control' backend is the calibration point: when every candidate fails a case there is no way to tell a hard case from a broken one. Point it at the strongest endpoint you have (a hosted model, or the LAN Ollama) and the benchmarks will flag a case the control also fails as suspect rather than as evidence about the candidates.

ollama.note: This stack's own service (docker-compose.yml). Native /api/tags too.

ollama-lan.note: Ollama on another host; see docker-compose.lan.yml.

geniex-npu.note: Snapdragon Hexagon NPU. QAIRT bundles only - loading a GGUF after a QAIRT bundle crashes the server.

geniex-gpu.note: Adreno GPU. Composes with the NPU lane at ~0% mutual cost.

geniex-cpu.note: Oryon CPU. Fastest GGUF backend here, but pegs 7.5 of 8 cores.

geniex-cpu-shim.note: PRE-0.6 ONLY. The CPU lane behind geniex_toolcall_shim.py. GenieX v0.6.0 added Qwen tool-call parsing, so on v0.6+ use geniex-cpu directly -- verified on v0.6.1, 2026-09-05. Keep this for older builds: without the shim they return Qwen's <tool_call> template as plain content and every tool call is invisible. Start it first: python3 geniex_toolcall_shim.py --upstream http://localhost:18184 --port 18190

geniex-hybrid.note: NPU+CPU. Slower than plain CPU on every model measured - avoid.

control.note: Calibration reference — see the comment above. Point this at the strongest endpoint available; a case the control also fails is a suspect case, not a model result.

mistral-glm.note: HOSTED, COSTS MONEY. The GLM-5.2 endpoint docs/mistral-vibe-glm-setup.md already configures for the coding agent, reused here as a strong control. Export MISTRAL_API_KEY first (console.mistral.ai/api-keys); the key never goes in this file. probe:false because a paid host should not be asked what it serves - the model id above is exact (zai-glm-5-2, not glm-5.2).
